sources.entry: React Native macOS - Build OS X desktop apps using React Native and Cocoa. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon] ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]](https://github.com/ptmt/react-native-desktop)

summary.one_liner: A fork of React Native for building macOS desktop applications with JavaScript and Cocoa, now unmaintained.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes React Native macOS (formerly react-native-desktop) as a way to build macOS desktop apps using React Native. It provides a CLI (react-native-macos-cli) that initializes a new project and runs it with a run-macos command. It can also add a macOS target to an existing iOS, Android, or Windows React Native project by merging the generated folder and adding an rn-cli.config.js file. Documentation is inherited from the React Native docs because the project is a fork. An RNTesterApp example set of component demos is included, and it can load external JavaScript bundles over HTTP. The README states the project is no longer maintained.
use_cases: build a macOS desktop app with JavaScript
reuse React Native code for a Mac app
add a macOS target to an existing React Native project
explore React Native components on macOS with RNTesterApp
load a JavaScript bundle over HTTP for testing
notable: Fork of React Native for iOS retargeted to macOS with Cocoa views
CLI can add a macOS target to an existing iOS, Android, or Windows React Native project
Inherits React Native documentation since it is a fork
RNTesterApp includes component examples and can load bundles from a URL
caveats: The project is no longer maintained (deprecation notice at top of README)
Described as fairly new; the author says to proceed at own risk
A Microsoft-maintained version and React Native on Catalyst are mentioned as alternatives
keywords: add macos to react native project
